title: GTA 6 pre-orders are ‘far above initial expectations’ but NBA 2K27 was ‘below our forecast’, Take-Two says | VGC
summary: NBA was still the second most successful launch in the series’ history…
text: GTA 6 pre-orders are ‘far above initial expectations’ but NBA 2K27 was ‘below our forecast’, Take-Two says | VGC Open main menu News Reviews Features Guides PlayStation Xbox Nintendo PC Gaming Mobile Login Zelda Gold Skulltulas Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides New Game Release Dates Search VGC Login with Patreon First for Video Game News Follow VGC GTA 6 pre-orders are ‘far above initial expectations’ but NBA 2K27 was ‘below our forecast’, Take-Two says NBA was still the second most successful launch in the series’ history, it says Video Game News 10th Nov 2026 / 10:01 am Posted by Chris Scullion Take-Two says pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are “far above initial expectations”, but its other recent major release NBA 2K27 hasn’t met its forecast. Despite delivering “the second highest net bookings performance in the history of the series” and selling more than 4 million copies since its release in early September, NBA 2K27 “was below our forecast for the period”, according to the publisher. It expects big things from GTA 6 , however, stating: “Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI are tracking far above our initial expectations, and we know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough.” Despite this claim, Take-Two has only modestly revised its forecast for the financial year, adjusting its range from $7.9 – $8.1 billion up to $7.98 – $8.18 billion. In an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said the company was not yet adjusting its guidance because the game is so close to release. “[We cannot] disclose the numbers, but the point that we’re making is our prior expectations obviously were aligned with our guidance, and the pre-orders are far exceeding our original expectations,” Zelnick said. “We’re maintaining our guidance, because the release is only 10 days away and we’ll know a lot more after the release.” When asked whether the decision to keep the guidance at around $8 billion for the year was a sign that Take-Two wasn’t predicting a bigger than expected launch, Zelnick reiterated: “We’re just not updating our numbers right now because we are so close to the launch. However, pre-orders are far exceeding our expectations.” Further reading Rockstar releases nearly 40 new GTA 6 screenshots ahead of launch Rockstar gives us a brand new look at GTA 6 Elsewhere in the interview, Zelnick was asked whether he felt the wave of live service games had passed. He replied that the vast majority of Take-Two’s income still comes from live service titles (such as GTA Online, NBA 2K or WWE 2K), the upcoming release of GTA aside. “We’ve said all along that free-to-play titles are very challenging, whether that’s in mobile or PC or console,” Zelnick explained. “But live service, I would say that’s too broad a brush, because live services are extremely successful. The bulk of our business is represented by live services and what we call recurrent consumer spend. It’s the vast majority of our business today.” He added: “The business basically runs on live services, punctuated by, we hope, some huge releases.” Post a comment Related VGC Content Rockstar announces Grand Theft Auto 6 music festival taking place in Miami 21 hours ago GTA 6 may be censored in Australia and other regions, dataminer suggests 21 hours ago Selfridges London has launched a huge Grand Theft Auto 6 store with 60+ items for sale 1 day ago Rockstar releases nearly 40 new GTA 6 screenshots ahead of launch 4 days ago We sometimes publish affiliate links on VGC.
